title: Architecture & Standards: API, Coding, Infra, Model-Serving, Observability, Performance, and ADRs
author: Erin McCarthy
content:
Summary:
This document consolidates Redwood Inference's canonical architecture and standards across API design, coding practices, infrastructure, model-serving, observability, performance targets, and the ADR (Architecture Decision Record) process. It is intended as the single-source-of-truth for engineers and product teams designing or modifying services that participate in the platform (hosted, dedicated, private).

Scope:
- Applies to all services owned by Redwood core platform and customer-facing inference runtimes.
- Audience: backend engineers, infra engineers, SRE, applied ML, product managers.
- Not a replacement for team-level runbooks; it defines company-wide constraints, requirements, and review processes.

Principles (high-level):
1. Predictability: APIs and infra must provide stable semantics and measurable SLOs.
2. Observability-first: instrumented by default for metrics, traces, and structured logs.
3. Production-first ergonomics: defaults favor safe deployments (circuit breakers, fallbacks).
4. Cost-awareness: design choices should consider per-token/per-request unit economics.
5. Backwards compatibility: follow explicit versioning and deprecation flows.

1) API Standards
Purpose: Ensure consistent, discoverable, and stable external and internal APIs.
Key rules:
- API style: RESTful JSON for external public endpoints; internal RPC (gRPC/HTTP/2) allowed for low-latency intra-cluster calls.
- Versioning: use semantic versioning in the route (e.g., /v1/generate). Breaking changes require an ADR + 90-day deprecation window for public APIs.
- Authentication: OAuth2 or mTLS for external integrations; service-to-service uses short-lived JWTs with rotating signing keys.
- Error model: 3xx/4xx/5xx semantics. Error body must follow standard envelope: {
  "error": {
    "code": "string",
    "message": "string",
    "details": ["optional strings"]
  }
}
- Idempotency: For any non-idempotent operation (long-running job, create), require an idempotency key header (Idempotency-Key).
- Pagination: cursor-based pagination (cursor + limit) for listing endpoints. Avoid offset for large datasets.
- Rate limits and quotas: documented per-route. Client-facing endpoints return headers: X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset.
- Schema: OpenAPI 3.1 spec required for all public APIs and internal RPC surface. Endpoint owners must publish a spec in the API spec repository and link in the service README.
- Contracts: maintain test suites that validate contract compatibility (consumer-driven contract testing) on every change.

API Design Checklist (must pass before review):
- [ ] OpenAPI spec updated
- [ ] Auth patterns validated (roles/scopes)
- [ ] Error codes documented and mapped to failures
- [ ] Backwards compatibility verified or ADR authored
- [ ] Perf budget defined (p95/p99 targets)

2) Coding Standards
Scope: server-side services and libraries that form Redwood runtime.
- Languages: primary backend languages are Go (server, infra) and Python (model tooling, evals). New languages require an engineering leadership sign-off.
- Style and linting: enable gofmt/golangci-lint for Go; black/flake8/isort for Python. CI must block merging on lint errors.
- Testing: unit coverage >= 60% for critical path code; integration tests required for API surface and data-plane changes.
- PR process: small, focused PRs; reviewers required: at least one owner and one cross-team reviewer for infra-impacting changes.
- Dependency management: use vetted registries; automated dependabot alerts must be triaged within 5 business days for security fixes.
- Secrets: never checked into source control. Use secrets manager (see Infra Standards).

3) Infrastructure Standards
Goal: reproducible, auditable, and secure infra across hosted/dedicated/private.
- IaC: Terraform (recommended) + Terragrunt patterns. State stored in encrypted S3 buckets with DynamoDB state locking.
- Environments: dev/staging/prod parity. All infra changes go through PR and staging deployment before prod.
- Networking: use VPCs with least-privilege security groups; customer-private deployments require documented network map and ingress whitelist.
- Secrets & Keys: AWS KMS/HSM for hosted; private deployments integrate with customer KMS if provided. Rotate keys quarterly.
- Build & Deploy: CI pipelines produce immutable artifacts (container images with digest). CD uses progressive rollouts (canary then linear).
- Ownership: every resource must have an oncall owner and cost center tag (owner:oncall-team, cost-center:product).

Mandatory Infra Table (minimum configs):
| Component | Minimum Requirement | Owner/Notes |
|----------|---------------------|------------|
| Terraform state | Encrypted S3 + DynamoDB locking | eng-infra |
| Container images | Signed, digest pinned in deploy | eng-platform |
| Secrets storage | KMS-backed secret manager | security-and-compliance |
| Networking | VPC, subnets by tier, NACLs/SGs | eng-infra |

4) Model-serving Standards
Purpose: Ensure safe, performant, and reproducible model deployments.
- Packaging: models stored in manifest-driven bundles (weights + config + tokenizer spec + quantization profile). Manifest must include model_id, version, architecture, and verified quantization profile.
- Model Registry: all production models registered in the model catalog with metadata: commit hash, training dataset id (if applicable), evaluation artifacts, privacy classification.
- Versioning and Rollouts: immutable model versions. Rollouts must use canary -> ramp -> full with metrics gating: quality evals, latency, error rate, cost delta.
- Quantization & Profiling: quantization profiles validated against a standard eval harness (perf and quality metrics) before being promoted. Profile metadata lives in quantization-profiles.
- KV Cache and Prefix Caching: runtime must expose cache hit/miss metrics and eviction policy; models with large KV requirements must document memory footprint and warm-up steps.
- Routing & Fallbacks: smart routing policies must be configured (latency-first, cost-first, region-first), and automatic fallback to compatible model variants implemented for capacity failures.
- Observability: per-model metrics (tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_p50/p95/p99, quality_regression_score) emitted as tagged metrics.

Model-serving Checklist:
- [ ] Model manifest in registry
- [ ] Quantization profile verified (if applicable)
- [ ] Canary plan and gating metrics defined
- [ ] Rollback plan and compatibility matrix attached

5) Observability Standards
Goals: fast debug, clear alerting, and SLO measurement.
- Metrics: export via Prometheus exposition format. Standard metric prefixes: redwood_ (counters), redwood_g_ (gauges), redwood_hist_ (histograms).
- Distributed Tracing: OpenTelemetry spans for request lifecycle (ingress -> model runtime -> storage). Trace context must be propagated across RPC boundaries.
- Logs: structured JSON logs with stable fields: service, env, request_id, user_id (if applicable), model_id, level, message. Logs written to central logging (ELK/Cloud logging).
- Dashboards: per-service golden signal dashboard: traffic, errors, latency, saturation. Model dashboards include quality and cost views.
- SLOs and Alerts: SLOs documented in SLO registry and associated alerts. Default alerting thresholds:
  - Page (sev1): sustained SLO breach > 15 minutes or error rate > 5% for 5m window
  - Pager (sev2): p95 latency > target for 10m or traffic spike leading to saturation
- Alerting playbooks: every alert must map to an ownership and runbook link. Pager duty rotations must be defined in eng-sre.

6) Performance Standards
Target: predictable latency and throughput with measurable unit economics.
- Latency targets (examples, adjust per product):
  - Text generation (hosted API): p50 < 60ms per-token, p95 < 250ms per-token, cold-start p99 < 2s for small models.
  - Embeddings: p95 < 150ms
  - Model inference timeouts: default 30s (configurable per-route)
- Throughput: services must define a throughput budget (requests/sec or tokens/sec) and document CPU/GPU requirements per model variant.
- Benchmarking: every model or infra change must include a benchmark run (standard perf-suite) with representative sequence lengths and batch distributions. Use benchmarking-and-perf-suite repository.
- Load testing: pre-production load tests for any change impacting traffic path or autoscaling rules. Runbooks for autoscaler tuning in eng-sre.
- Performance regression protection: CI must run perf smoke tests and block deploys with >10% regression in key metrics.

7) Decision Records (ADRs)
Purpose: capture non-trivial architecture decisions and rationale.
Process:
1. When a design choice affects cross-team contracts or is a breaking change, author an ADR using the template.
2. ADR must include: title, date, status (proposed/accepted/deprecated), context, decision, consequences, alternatives considered, testing plan, owner.
3. Review: at least two reviewers from affected teams and one architecture steward.
4. Publication: store ADR as a markdown file in the ADR directory and link in the related service README.
5. Deprecation: when superseded, update ADR status to deprecated with link to successor ADR.

ADR Template (text):
- Title: Short descriptive title
- Authors: list of authors
- Date: YYYY-MM-DD
- Status: proposed | accepted | deprecated | superseded
- Context and Problem Statement:
- Decision Drivers:
- Considered Options:
- Decision Outcome:
- Consequences (pros/cons):
- Implementation Plan and Rollout Steps:
- Monitoring and Rollback Plan:

Governance and Ownership
- Standards steward: eng-platform is the primary steward for infra and deployment patterns.
- API steward: eng-developer-experience maintains API contract requirements.
- Model steward: applied-ml-and-evals maintains model-serving, quantization, and eval policies.
- SRE steward: eng-sre maintains SLO/alerting defaults and runbooks.
- Process steward: architecture-and-standards team maintains this document and coordinates periodic reviews (quarterly).

Enforcement and Exceptions
- Exceptions: team leads may request exceptions via a short ADR; exceptions must include mitigating controls and an expiration date.
- Auditing: security-and-compliance will perform annual audits for infra and model-serving compliance; findings tracked in risk-and-exceptions.

Appendices
A. Example error response (standardized):
{
  "error": {
    "code": "rate_limit_exceeded",
    "message": "Rate limit exceeded. See X-RateLimit-Reset header.",
    "details": ["limit: 60 req/min"]
  }
}

B. Quick rollout checklist for model change:
1. Author ADR if cross-team or breaking.
2. Publish model manifest to registry.
3. Run quantization/profile benchmarks.
4. Deploy canary (1-5% traffic) and run evals for quality/latency/cost.
5. Monitor gating metrics for 1 hour min or 10k requests.
6. Ramp to 25%, then 50%, then 100% with metric gates.
7. Record rollout in release notes and tag owner oncall.

C. Useful links:
- API spec repo: /repos/api-specs (internal)
- Model registry: /applied-ml-and-evals/model-onboarding (internal)
- ADR directory: /architecture-and-standards/decision-records (internal)
- Perf suite: /eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite (internal)
